title: Org Settings: Compact Access Center — sketch + interaction notes
content:
Context / problem statement:
We need a compact, fast-access UI surface for org and team access controls that surfaces the most common tasks (rotate keys, preview effective permissions, suspend service accounts, view recent audit events) without forcing users into deep settings pages. Current flows are too many clicks for frequent ops (on-call engineers, platform integrators, security reviews).

Goals:
- Single-pane quick actions for common tasks while preserving access to full detailed views.
- Make RBAC readable at-a-glance for non-admins (who can read) and actionable for admins (who can act).
- Inline audit snippet: allow triage and jump-to-context to the full audit timeline.
- Performance at scale: support orgs with 1000+ teams and 50k+ API keys without freezing listing views.
- Meet baseline security constraints: no plaintext secrets in UI, require MFA for destructive actions.

Primary users:
- Platform engineers (create/rotate keys, inspect service accounts)
- Security reviewers (audit events, permission drift)
- Team admins (invite users, assign roles)
- On-call engineers (quickly disable compromised service accounts)

Design constraints / principles:
- Compact cards + progressive disclosure. Cards represent teams/service-accounts/api-key groups.
- Hover-to-preview/policy-inspector for RBAC entries (no modal navigation).
- Keyboard-first operations: quick search, enter to open, cmd-k to global actions.
- Throttle heavy operations (full permission eval) and show cached preview with refresh button.

High-level layout (single pane with contextual panel):
- Left: Org/team quick filter + saved filters (Teams / My keys / Recently active)
- Middle: Compact card grid/list (team card or SA card) with key summary
- Right: Context panel (drawer) for details, actions, and audit snippet

ASCII wireframe (compact list mode):
[Org Filter] | [Team / SA list (compact rows)]               | [Context panel]
----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------
- Search    | Team: payments                                 | Team: payments         
- Saved Filt|  •  payments-admins  (3 admins)  •  12 keys     | Last 3 events          
- Tags     |  •  payments-prod     (svc acct)  •  4 keys      | • KEY_ROTATED 10m ago  
           |  •  payments-observers (read-only)            | • SA_DISABLED 2d ago    

Card contents (row):
- Left: icon (team / sa / key group), name, team owner(s)
- Middle: small KPI chips: active keys, last activity, open incidents
- Right: quick action icons: rotate key, suspend SA, open policy-preview (hover), open audit snippet

Context panel sections (top->bottom):
1) Summary header: name, type, last modified by, quick-action primary button (e.g., Rotate Primary Key)
2) Effective permissions preview: small matrix 3x3 (resources x verbs) with color-coded cells and tooltip to view exact policies. Non-admins see read-only.
3) Keys table/compact list: API key id (truncated), created, last used, status, actions (revoke, copy-id, request-rotate). Copy requires confirmation modal for sensitive ops.
4) Service account credentials: list of attached keys & KMS/HSM indicator. Button: Request short-lived token.
5) Audit snippet: latest 5 events (compact rows) with a small timeline sparkline and filter chips (actor, event type, resource). Each event has a "jump" link to full audit history (opens complete audit page filtered).
6) Safety controls: escalation checkbox, require MFA toggle for destructive ops, canary rollout switch (for team-level policy changes)

Interaction notes / micro-behaviors:
- Hover policy inspector: on hover over a permission cell show which policies contributed (inline list of policy names with origin: org/team/service-account). Click policy name to open a focused policy editor in the right panel.
- Permission preview fallback: calculating exact effective permissions is expensive. Show a cached preview + an inline "Refresh exact permissions" button that displays a spinner and updates. Limit refresh rate per user (2/min) to prevent thundering herd.
- Quick rotate flow: clicking rotate => small inline wizard in context panel (step 1: select key to rotate; step 2: choose rotation method (zero-downtime via new key + dual-signed grace window or immediate switch); step 3: require justification (log) + optional notification email). After rotate, show audit event and ephemeral banner with rollback option for 10 minutes.
- Suspend SA: immediate UI feedback, revoke active tokens (call to backend revocation endpoint). Require typed confirmation for org-level SAs.
- Search and global shortcuts: cmd-k opens command palette with actions (e.g., "Rotate key payments-prod:primary").

Edge cases and scalability considerations:
- Organizations with nested teams: show flattened list by default with breadcrumb for parent team in card. Allow "group by parent" toggle.
- Cross-team service accounts: SA can be attached to multiple teams; in card show "attached to X teams" badge and allow to open a small membership overlay.
- Lots of keys: lazy load keys table with server-side pagination + cursor. Keep top-level cards lightweight (just counts).
- Very active audit logs: the snippet should be windowed (last 5) with a link to query the full log in the audit console (not recommended to pull full history in-line). Provide server-side summary metrics (counts by event type).

Security + compliance notes:
- Never show raw secret values in UI. For new keys, provide a one-time download/clipboard copy with an explicit indicator ("this is the only time to copy the secret").
- Sensitive operations require 2FA confirmation for owners or users with specific security flags.
- All destructive actions create linked Jira tickets optionally via integration (checkbox in rotate/suspend flows).

Accessibility notes:
- Ensure keyboard-only users can operate the quick action icons via focus and confirm with Enter.
- Color-coded permission cells should include textual labels and aria-live updates for permission changes.

Backlog / engineering TODOs (rough priorities):
1) MVP: compact list + context drawer with keys table + audit snippet (P0)
   - Acceptance: rotate key flow works end-to-end, audit snippet links to full audit, mobile-friendly collapse.
2) Policy hover inspector + cached/eager eval (P1)
3) Canary rollout toggle + rollback affordance (P1)
4) Saved filters & keyboard palette (P2)
5) Cross-team membership overlay + nested-team grouping (P2)
6) KMS/HSM metadata integration in SA view (P3)

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Should we allow copy of API key IDs without MFA? (proposal: copy ID allowed; copy secret requires MFA + short TTL)
- Rollback UX: how long to offer rollback after rotate? (proposal: 10 minutes default, config per org)
- Role previews for non-admins: should we mask certain policy origins? (proposal: show origin but redact policy ids for external auditors)

Notes for follow-up research / usability tests:
- Observe engineers performing key rotation during incidents: measure time-to-rotate and friction points.
- Test hover policy inspector: does it reduce navigation to policy editor?
- Validate audit snippet usefulness: show to 5 SREs, 5 security reviewers — capture usage and whether they click through to full audit console.

Related references/links:
- Confluence: Org ACL and Policy Evaluation (CONFLUENCE-ORG-ACL-485)
- Jira: PLAT-1234 (compact access center spike)
- Slack thread: #product-console: thread with initial sketches (link above)

Next steps / immediate actions:
- Share this doc with Marco + Renee for initial UX review (ask: focus on permission preview legibility).
- Build a quick Figma sketch for the compact card + context panel and run a 30-minute design crit on 2025-11-18.
- Engineering spike: measurement of cost to calculate exact effective permissions for orgs with 20k principals (assign to Diego; 3 days).

-- end of notes --
